searchText: There was some interesting discussion around not having a queue at all, which would also be attractive, but I agree that it's probably close to time that we just get on with it... I think if we do sweeping withdrawals the non-queue implementation seems really nice. I think I'd still slightly prefer the original 2 loop implementation because I think the prioritization of the full withdrawals is really nice because those are voluntary (ignoring slashing) and just larger sums locked up - and there's a tangible cost there. I also haven't been involved in the actual implementation for us so I'll also have to defer on the technical implications of each a bit here +1 for not wanting to delay capella regardless though Just because it was on telegram but i feel like this is a better place to capture everything - there was never a stated requirement to prioritise full over partial, i did ask specifically - the single loop was more around offering a minimal viable solution... but the lack of queue would make that simpler again - was pretty much an agreement around not getting into the 'fairness' discussion as thats not really my wheel house And now Im onto reading <@755590043632140352> PR https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3068 on same topic POLL: Should it be considered a 'requirement' that full withdrawals be prioritised over partial withdrawals when processing withdrawals? Please react with ✅ (Tick mark) = Yes, ❌ (Cross) = no

I also haven't been involved in the actual implementation for us so I'll also have to defer on the technical implications of each a bit here 

+1 for not wanting to delay capella regardless though
